subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Geneva Mechanism: Step by Step
description: A fast breakdown of Geneva Mechanism: Step by Step for builders.

hook.text: A wheel that turns in exact, equal steps — not smoothly — has a use.

buildup.text: A pin on a driving disc enters slots in a second wheel and rotates it one step.

discovery.text: The number of slots sets the step size. Four slots give quarter turns.

twist.text: Between steps, a locking disc holds the output perfectly still — no drift.

climax.text: Film projectors used Geneva drives to advance film one frame at a time.

punchline.text: Move, stop, move, stop — precise indexing in a tiny package.

quiz.question: How does a Geneva mechanism hold the output stationary between steps?
options: A brake pad clamps the output disc
A locking disc on the driver blocks the output slots between pin entries
Friction in the bearings holds it in place naturally
